2337.resolution: Round 1: both reviewers read 'increatam' as 'uncreated'. Held after a second check against the Latin: 'increatam animae nostrae a Deo' has a dative ('in our soul') and an agent ('by God'), and the clause goes on 'vel eandem cum charitatis habitu, vel distinctam ab eodem' (the same as the created habit of charity, or distinct from it). This is the scholastic created habit Pighius rejects, so the word is read as the participle of 'increo' ('created in'). An 'uncreated' quality made by God would contradict the sentence. The English now shows the Latin word ('created in (increatam) our soul by God'), with a note. Kimi's other points were rejected: 'senses' renders 'acceptionem', as in the locus title; 'his work' is supplied for 'libro quinto de Libero Arbitrio'. Round 2: both reviewers repeat the 'uncreated' reading. Rejected on the same grounds, and reported to Stephan as a judgment call. Checked clause by clause against the Latin; the English keeps the sense, agents, negations and modality of the source. Re-reviewed after the fix.

Revision review, scope §2337 only. Both reviewers again read 'increatam' as 'uncreated'. Rejected on the sources. Pighius's own text, De libero hominis arbitrio et divina gratia (Cologne, 1542), lib. 5, fol. 76r (archive.org bub_gb_nGsCu5n-cH4C), reads: 'Quandoquidem, in illis [the schools], fere imaginantur gratiam Dei qualitatem aliquam increatam animae nostrae a Deo: vel eandem cum charitatis habitu, vel distinctam ab eodem. Quae commentitia universa existimo.' Bellarmine, De gratia et libero arbitrio 1.3 (Vives ed., vol. 5; archive.org operaomnia05bell), quotes the same words, including 'increatam'. In that chapter he defends the view Pighius attacks as 'habitum supernaturalem a Deo nobis infundi, quo anima exornetur' and grace as 'habitum, sive qualitatem creatam', and he groups Pighius with Calvin's 'gratuita acceptione nos esse justos'. So the word describes the schools' infused created quality, which Pighius rejects in favour of grace as God's favour. In scholastic usage 'gratia increata' is God's favour or the Holy Spirit (Le Blanc Thesis II; Lombard, Sent. 1 d. 17), and no scholastic calls the infused quality uncreated. 'Increatam ... a Deo' is the participle of 'increo' ('created in ... by God'). English kept; the notes now cite this evidence. Kimi's other points are stylistic: 'of some fame' for 'non incelebris'; 'senses' for 'acceptionem', as in the locus title; 'generally' for 'fere'; 'invented' for 'commentitia'. Checked clause by clause against the Latin; the English keeps the sense, agents, negations and modality of the source. Re-reviewed after the fix.
